tieu_de: Pluto transit through the 12th house: what was buried comes up to be healed
mo: Why do I feel so tired of social life right now?
Is it normal for old memories to keep coming back?
How does this transit connect to Pluto entering the 1st house?

Before Pluto reaches your Ascendant and starts remaking your outward life, it passes through the 12th house. This is the quiet, hidden part of the chart, and here the work happens mostly out of sight. Old memories, fears you put away, patterns you never looked at directly all begin to rise.
It is not always comfortable. It is, though, one of the most healing transits you can have, because it lets you deal with things at the root rather than trimming the branches.

doan: The 12th house governs the unconscious, solitude, retreat, dreams, hidden fears and the places where people withdraw from the world, such as hospitals, retreats and monasteries. Pluto transforms by bringing buried things to light. In this house, the buried things are inside you.
The work is inner and often private. What you clear here prepares the ground for the more visible reinvention that comes when Pluto crosses into the 1st house.
Planet Pluto Rules Scorpio Transformation, rebirth, power

Dreams may become vivid and repetitive. Memories you had not thought about for years return without warning. You might find yourself reacting strongly to situations that echo something from long ago, then realise the reaction belongs to the past.
Many people feel a stronger need for time alone. Crowds become tiring and quiet becomes necessary. Some go on retreats, start meditating seriously, or spend more time reading and reflecting.
Intuition often sharpens. You pick up on things about yourself and others that you cannot fully explain but that turn out to be accurate.

This is an ideal time for inner work. Psychotherapy, support groups, reflective reading and any practice aimed at inner development can be especially rewarding now. Wounds that seemed permanent can finally heal.

With willpower strongly engaged, you can change old patterns at their source. People who use this transit well often describe feeling reborn, not dramatically, but in a steady, grounded way that lasts.

The hidden nature of this house means much of what happens is hard to talk about. It is easy to feel alone with it. Buried material can surface at inconvenient times and bring waves of feeling that seem out of proportion to the moment.
There is also a temptation to avoid the process: staying busy, numbing out, or retreating so far that you lose contact with support. Pluto tends to press harder when it is ignored.

Pluto spends 12 to 30 years in a sign, and a house transit usually runs on a similar scale. Depending on your house system and birth latitude, your 12th house may be larger or smaller, so this chapter may be shorter or longer. As Pluto approaches the Ascendant at the end of the 12th house, retrograde motion can bring it close to that threshold several times before it crosses.
Find a good therapist or counsellor if you do not have one. This transit rewards having a trusted guide for the inner work.
Keep a dream journal or a simple daily notebook. Writing down what comes up helps you see patterns and makes the material less overwhelming.
Build regular time for solitude into your week, and protect it. At the same time, stay connected to a few people you trust.
Stop pushing difficult memories away every time they surface. Start giving them a little attention in a safe setting, and notice how they lose their grip over time.
The 12th house pulls attention inward. Pluto intensifies that pull because there is important inner work to do. Needing more solitude is normal during this transit and is usually temporary.
Yes. Pluto in the 12th house is known for bringing up buried memories and feelings so they can be resolved. If they become overwhelming, professional support makes a real difference.

The 12th house transit is the preparation. The inner clearing done now makes the outer reinvention of the 1st house transit steadier and more authentic. People who do this work often find the next chapter less turbulent.
